comment: B2 Round 24 — redaction reducer × history_visibility composition vectors. Spec authority: data-structures/redaction.md + data-structures/history-visibility.md + authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md. The redaction reducer produces a tombstone (kind=ak.message.redact) that supersedes the target event; history_visibility (cell ak.component.realm.history_visibility.v1) controls who SEES a redacted event vs a fully-removed event vs the original. Authors of the redacted event ALWAYS see it (consent + audit). Members see the tombstone only. world_readable visibility removes the event entirely (no tombstone surface) since non-members cannot prove membership consent. Reverse-redaction is a Move that removes the tombstone (causal or-set remove of the redaction op_id), re-exposing the original.

vectors.name: tombstone_visible_to_author
vectors.comment: Author of the original event ALWAYS sees the tombstone with the original content displayed via the audit_view (the author's own consent surface). Visibility setting is irrelevant for authors.

expected.rationale: Authors see the audit-view of their own redactions; original body remains visible.

vectors.name: tombstone_visible_to_member_content_hidden
vectors.comment: Members of the space see the tombstone (a redaction marker with no body) but NOT the original content. Visibility=shared means joined+invited members can see history.

expected.rationale: Members see the tombstone but content is stripped; member learns the message existed and was redacted.

vectors.name: world_readable_visibility_redaction_fully_removes
vectors.comment: When history_visibility=world_readable, the space is publicly readable; redaction must REMOVE the entire event (including tombstone) — no record visible to non-members. Authors still see via author_audit; world readers see nothing where the event used to be.

expected.rationale: world_readable: non-members have no membership consent surface to anchor an audit trail to; the redaction reducer must fully remove the event for non-author non-members.

vectors.name: reverse_redaction_re_exposes_original
vectors.comment: A reverse-redaction Move (ak.message.unredact) issues a causal or_set_remove against the redaction op_id; the original event must be re-exposed. The history_visibility setting governs the post-revert view in the same way the pre-redaction view was governed.

expected.rationale: Causal or-set remove of the redaction op_id; original event re-exposed under prevailing history_visibility.

vectors.name: joined_visibility_member_sees_tombstone
vectors.comment: history_visibility=joined: only currently-joined members see history. A joined member sees the redaction tombstone (no body) just like the shared case.

expected.rationale: Joined-only visibility: members see tombstone, body stripped.
